35 The diagram shows part of a circuit that uses a potentiometer wire to measure a potential
difference (p.d.) in an external circuit.
E
I1
L1
X
Z
Y
L2
I2
P
Q
The potentiometer wire XZ has length L1. It is connected to a cell of known electromotive force
(e.m.f.) E that has negligible internal resistance.
Terminals P and Q are connected to the external p.d. to be measured. The length of the
potentiometer wire between points X and Y is L2.
The ratio of the lengths L1 and L2 is used to determine the p.d. between P and Q in terms of E.
Which condition must be met in order to determine this p.d.?
A
The current I1 must be zero.
B
The current I2 must be zero.
C
The p.d. across YZ must be zero.
D
The resistance of the external circuit must be zero.

hints: Notice that terminal P joins X and terminal Q joins the sliding contact Y, so the unknown p.d. is placed across wire length $L_2$.
Recall that the wire XZ has total p.d. $E$ across total length $L_1$, so p.d. per unit length is uniform only if only $I_1$ flows in XZ.
Consider what happens to the p.d. across XY if some current $I_2$ leaves X for the external circuit instead of all current staying in the wire.
walkthrough: Identify the two loops: driver cell $E$ drives current $I_1$ through uniform wire XZ of length $L_1$, and terminals P-Q connect the unknown p.d. across section XY of length $L_2$.

State the potentiometer principle: for a uniform wire, resistance is proportional to length, so with constant $I_1$ the p.d. across a section is proportional to its length, $V_{XY} = I_1 \times \rho L_2/A$ and $E = I_1 \times \rho L_1/A$.
Require the null condition: if current $I_2$ flows in the test branch, $I_1$ splits at X and the wire current changes, so $V_{XY}$ no longer equals the simple fraction of $E$.
Set $I_2 = 0$ so no current is drawn from the circuit under test and the full $I_1$ stays in XZ, giving $V_{XY}/E = L_2/L_1$.
Then the external p.d. $V_{PQ}$ equals $V_{XY}$ at balance, so $V_{PQ} = E \times L_2/L_1$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Current $I_1$ must flow through wire XZ to maintain the uniform potential gradient with total p.d. $E$ across $L_1$.

B.explanation: When $I_2 = 0$ no current is drawn from the test circuit, so p.d. across XY equals the external p.d. and $V_{PQ} = E \times L_2/L_1$.

C.explanation: The p.d. across YZ is $E \times (L_1 - L_2)/L_1$, which is not zero unless $L_2 = L_1$.

D.explanation: Zero external resistance would short P to Q and would not give the balance condition; the potentiometer must draw no current.
